YOU
Use your inspectWellLog tool on the attached LAS file and report the depth range, the curves with units, and any data-quality issues. Then use crossplotWellLog with x=DFAR and y=NEUT.
PAPYRUS
I'll inspect the LAS file first, then run the crossplot.

◫ Well-log crossplot ↗
PAPYRUS
Well log inspection — Scorpio E1
Source: …/Library/Uploads/73b321fbcc56d844bc71918172ce2baab98eebc096221428f2691878586c2c4a-89c7dd2f-scorpio-e1-mt-eba-borehole-6038187.las
Header: WELL = Scorpio E1 · UWI 6038-187 · LOC = Mt Eba · DATE 15/03/2015 · STRT 0.050 · STOP 136.600 · STEP 0.050 · NULL −99999 · 2,732 rows.
Depth range
0.05 m to 136.60 m (DEPT, unit M), regularly sampled at 0.05 m — roughly 136.6 m of section in 2,732 rows.
Curves with units
MNEMONIC	UNIT	MIN	MAX	VALID ROWS
DEPT	M	0.05	136.6	2732
CALI	MM	−56.28	103.38	2732
DFAR	G/CM3	0.725	5.989	2701
DNEAR	G/CM3	0.657	3.382	2701
GAMN	GAPI	−2324.28	169.67	2691
NEUT	CPS	81.00	1666.0	2492
PR	OHM/M	115.51	50499.9	2692
SP	MV	−3.049	102.90	2692
COND	MS/M	−117.00	4978.16	2697
Data-quality issues (these are genuine, from the values themselves)
Extensive null runs at both ends of the log. NEUT, PR, SP, COND, GAMN, DFAR and DNEAR all carry nulls over roughly the first ~5 m and the last ~2.5 m. The logging suite effectively starts near 5 m and ends near 134.3 m, even though the header claims 0.05–136.60 m.
NEUT is the sparsest curve — 2,492 valid of 2,732 (240 nulls, ~8.8%). It also splits into two clearly different populations: ~550–1,665 CPS in the upper/earlier part of the run and then ~81–400 CPS over the deeper logged interval. That step is a tool/scale condition change, not geology.
Constant sentinel values masquerading as data. CALI = 49.765 MM repeated for the top 86 samples; DFAR = 4.587 G/CM3 repeated at top and bottom; DNEAR = 3.382 G/CM3 repeated; GAMN = −2324.28 GAPI repeated (a null-coded value that did not match the declared NULL of −99999, so it was read as a real number and drove GAMN's negative minimum); PR = 115.508 OHM/M repeated; SP = −3.049 MV repeated. These are pre-logging filler, not measurements.
Sensor spikes. CALI drops to −56.275 mm (physically impossible caliper) and spikes to 103.38 mm; PR hits the 50,499.9 Ω·m rail for long stretches (a saturated/rail value, not resistance); COND contains negative values down to −116.998 mS/m (non-physical). GAMN's −2324.28 GAPI floor reflects the same issue.
DFAR envelope outliers. DFAR ranges 0.725–5.989 g/cm³, where 5.989 g/cm³ exceeds any real formation density — the 4.587 sentinel is the culprit. DNEAR's 3.382 g/cm³ top-of-log constant is likewise implausible as rock.
Nulls are not uniformly distributed, so any depth-by-depth multi-curve comparison silently drops different intervals per curve — the crossplot below keeps only 1,246 of 2,732 rows.
Crossplot: DFAR (x) vs NEUT (y)
Plot rendered in the Crossplot view. Axis ranges: DFAR 0.725 → 2.207 g/cm³ (linear), NEUT 81.0 → 1,607 CPS (linear).
Plotted points: 1,246 — the tool thinned the log to every 2nd sample (2,732 rows) and kept only depths where both curves have values.
Pearson r = −0.572 (n = 1,246, both axes linear).
Shape: the cloud is broad and largely unstructured — not a single tight hyperbolic trend. There is a dense low-NEUT cluster (roughly 80–400 CPS) spread across the whole DFAR span, plus a separate higher-NEUT band (≈550–1,600 CPS) at lower DFAR. The split tracks the NEUT scale change noted above rather than a clean density–neutron response, which is why r is moderate and negative (negative being the conventional direction for this pairing).
Caveats the tool flags: the statistic is descriptive of the plotted samples only, on linear–linear axes, and is not a validated relationship. It is also computed on a thinned sample and on data containing the sentinels, rails and nulls listed above — most notably the DFAR 4.587 constant and the PR/CALI spikes — so treat r as indicative, not as a calibrated density–neutron cross-plot.
No lithology, porosity or other interpretation has been inferred; these are the measured values and their quality only.
